analyst_view.overall: Slovan Bratislava are bottom of the league phase with no points and a 1-17 goal record, and have lost 12 European games in a row, though they beat Ruzomberok 1-0 on Saturday under coach Yaya Toure; captain Sporar calls Betis 'the clear favourite'. Slovan are without winger Suleiman Camara and defender Kevin Wimmer, and Artur Gajdos is a doubt with knee pain. Betis are 11th on 9 points and 4th in La Liga after a 1-1 derby draw with Sevilla; Ceballos and Morante are out (counted), Lo Celso is also reported out after discomfort in training, and Antony is fit after a knock. Pellegrini is expected to rotate, with Troy Parrott starting up front and Cucho Hernandez on the bench. French referee Jerome Brisard, about average on cards, is in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals, including about 1.0 for Slovan, who have scored once in four Champions League games and now miss Camara, one of their few wide threats; their ratings lean on domestic results that flatter them at this level. Betis rotate after the derby, with Parrott up front instead of Cucho and Lo Celso also out, which takes a little off their side too. I keep the trim: 3.2 x 0.95, about 3.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners, with Betis around 6.1 and their busy recent corner counts already in (+3%). Even a rotated Betis should dominate the ball through Antony and Abde on the wings while Slovan defend deep, as Toure expects, and that is already in both records, so I stay at 9.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.7 cards, reflecting Slovan's usual card rate when chasing the ball, and Jerome Brisard's about-average record is already counted. Toure noted Betis are technical rather than physical, and nothing points to a more heated game than usual, so I stay at 4.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.8 shots and add about 11% to Betis for how much Slovan concede. Slovan's own shooting at this level has been thin, with Camara out and Gajdos doubtful, and a rotated Betis without Lo Celso may play at a lower tempo once ahead. A slight trim: 31.8 x 0.97, about 30.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.5 shots on target, including a 6% boost for Betis. Slovan rarely test goalkeepers in this competition, which their domestic-based ratings overstate, and Betis start with some second-choice attackers such as Parrott, so I go to 10.5 x 0.96, about 10.1.
